title: BGSU women's basketball edges Western Michigan in back-and-forth battle - NewsBreak
text:
By BLADE STAFF ,
3 hours ago
BOWLING GREEN — In a game that saw a total of six lead changes in the second half, the Bowling Green State University women’s basketball team had the upper hand at the end, beating Western Michigan 67-63 at the Stroh Center on Wednesday.
The Falcons improved to 14-12 overall and 6-8 in the Mid-American Conference after the victory.
Western Michigan (7-17, 3-10 MAC) got a pair of 3-pointers from Alli Harness that put the visitors ahead 54-50 with 7:32 remaining. BGSU responded as Johnea Donahue converted a three-point play, Kaia Woods made a layup off an assist from Donahue, and Jasmine Fearne’s 3-pointer made it 58-54 Falcons with 5:30 left.
The Broncos’ De’Ahna Richardson answered with a 3 on their next possession, and the contest remained a one-possession game until the very end.
Donahue helped the Falcons close it out by going 6-for-6 from the foul line over the final 1:01. She finished with 14 points, six rebounds, and six steals.
Bowling Green led for all of the first half, albeit slightly, as it carried a 25-23 edge into the locker room. Neither team led by more than eight points throughout, the Broncos’ largest lead being four points and the Falcons eight.
Bowling Green forced Western Michigan into 21 turnovers while the Falcons committed 12. BGSU also had a slight edge in rebounding, 37-35.
For the game, the Falcons shot 37 percent (22 of 60) from the floor and 32 percent (6 of 19) from 3. The Broncos shot 42 percent (20 of 48) and 37 percent (10 of 27) from 3.
Paige Kohler finished with a game-high 16 points for BGSU. Taya Ellis added 13 points and 10 rebounds.
Western Michigan had double-figure scoring efforts from Richardson who had 13 points, Harness scored 12 points, and Kailey Starks finished with 11 points.
Bowling Green next hosts Toledo at 2 p.m. Saturday for the second game of the women’s Battle of I-75 rivalry series.
